samples.rationale: buildSpecialtyDirectory() puts the whole inversion rule — grouping, full-name formatting, ordering — inside VetController, which the catalog's Web controller row forbids and which the brief explicitly says is 'a fresh violation, not covered by the existing one'; a stateless domain service (Available, not currently used) fits, and the /specialties.html surface arguably belongs in its own Controller rather than bolted onto VetController. The nested SpecialtyDirectoryEntry record leaks to tests. holdersBySpecialtyId.get(specialty.getId()).add(vet) NPEs for any specialty not returned by findSpecialties, and the manual sort duplicates the query's ORDER BY. Tests are behavior-named and use factories, but rely on Mockito stubs, raw literals ("radiology", "Helen Leary"), substring HTML matching, narration comments, and no unit-level test.

VetController.buildSpecialtyDirectory embeds the whole inversion rule — seeding entries, filing vets, full-name formatting, dual ordering — in a web controller, a fresh violation of the 'no business rule in a controller' bar when the sanctioned Domain service pattern was available without an ADR; the logic is also unit-testable but every test boots MockMvc. It re-sorts a list the @Query already orders by name, and holdersBySpecialtyId.get(...).add(vet) NPEs on any specialty absent from findSpecialties(). The template's #{specialties} key ships with no message bundle. Tests are well named and factory-built, but narrate setup in comments ('// The mock returns...'), assert order via raw HTML substrings, and prove 'one page' only by attributeDoesNotExist("totalPages"). PRD and contracts table are updated.
